title: Compliance sprint report: RBACv2 & evidence pipeline impact analysis
body:
Executive summary:

This sprint-level report captures the current state of control alignment between SOC 2 / ISO 27001 requirements and our RBAC v2, audit log schema, and automated evidence pipeline. It synthesizes recent interviews with platform, SRE, and product engineers, summarizes discovered gaps, and proposes pragmatic remediation workstreams (with owners, scope, and acceptance criteria) tailored for the upcoming compliance audit window.

Scope and objectives:
- Controls in scope: Access control (A.9/CC6), Logging and monitoring (A.12/CC7), Change management (A.14/CC8), System configuration and baseline (A.8/CC5).
- Tech areas examined: RBAC v2 implementation (policy model + role hierarchy), audit log schema and retention pipeline, SIEM export format and saved queries, evidence automation playbooks and S3 evidence buckets.
- Objective: Provide clear remediation backlog that converts technical gaps into auditable artifacts and automation items.

Summary of findings (short):
- RBAC v2: Strong role model and policy language, but missing consistent role-to-control mapping artifacts (i.e., a machine-readable mapping showing which roles satisfy which SOC2/ISO controls).
- Audit logs: Core events captured (authn, authz decisions, admin changes, token issuance), but inconsistent field normalization across services and intermittent missing request_id propagation causing evidence gaps during multi-hop workflows.
- Evidence automation: Playbooks exist (Jenkins + lambda) but rely on manual triggers for several artifacts; end-to-end evidence collection for Dedicated and Private deployments not yet fully automated (edge buckets).
- SIEM export: Exports meet schema but several important predicates are missing from saved dashboards (no canonical saved query for "admin policy change" across services).

Detailed gaps and impact (ranked):
1) Control mapping artifact missing (Priority: P0)
   - Gap: No single, discoverable mapping file linking RBAC roles to SOC2/ISO control IDs and evidence sources.
   - Impact: Auditors request role-to-control traceability. Without it, interviews become manual and take longer (~4-6 hours per control).
   - Quick win: Produce a CSV mapping roles -> control IDs -> example evidence paths (owner: Maya Patel, ETA: 1 week).

2) Event normalization and request_id propagation (Priority: P0)
   - Gap: Some services (console-and-tooling, solutions-engineering) do not attach global_request_id consistently.
   - Impact: Reconstructing multi-service change events fails in 15-20% of sampled cases.
   - Remediation: Instrument global_request_id middleware in platform-service templates; backfill missing correlations via SIEM enrichment pipeline (owner: Ethan Li, ETA: 3 sprints).

3) Admin change saved queries in SIEM (Priority: P1)
   - Gap: No single saved query that reliably surfaces RBAC policy changes, role assignments, and config rollouts across environments.
   - Impact: Auditor proof requires manual joins across dashboards.
   - Remediation: Create standardized saved queries and a composite dashboard; add to audit evidence kit (owner: Jasper Nguyen, ETA: 2 weeks).

4) Evidence pipeline gaps for Dedicated & Private (Priority: P1)
   - Gap: Automated ingestion for on-prem evidence lives in a separate backlog and occasionally requires VPN-level access to fetch logs.
   - Impact: Slower evidence packaging for enterprise customers; additional manual steps escalate audit timelines.
   - Remediation: Extend evidence-extract lambda to support scheduled SFTP pulls and signed-presigned uploads from air-gapped customers; add acceptance tests (owner: Lina Kowalski, ETA: 4 sprints).

Remediation playbook (actionable items):
- Playbook item A: Role-to-control CSV + Markdown narrative (owner: Maya Patel)
  - Deliverable: roles-control-mapping.csv, README.md with mapping rationale, links to role definitions in infra repo.
  - Acceptance: Auditor can be shown mapping and role creation flow in a 20 minute demo.

- Playbook item B: Global_request_id enforcement (owner: Ethan Li)
  - Deliverable: middleware library bump, PRs across 6 services, SIEM enrichment job to correlate orphaned events.
  - Acceptance: >=95% successful cross-service correlation in production logs for the last 7 days.

- Playbook item C: SIEM saved queries + dashboard (owner: Jasper Nguyen)
  - Deliverable: saved queries for admin_change, role_assignment, token_issuance, and a "control-evidence" dashboard.
  - Acceptance: Queries return expected incidents in prepopulated test dataset; dashboard linked in evidence index.

- Playbook item D: Evidence pipeline extension for Dedicated/Private (owner: Lina Kowalski)
  - Deliverable: automated collectors, test harness, runbook describing data handling and encryption-in-transit.
  - Acceptance: Successful automated run for 2 closed-customer tenants (staging) with S3 evidence object in approved bucket.

Auditor-facing Q&A (prep notes and suggested responses):
- Q: "How are role changes tracked and who approves them?"
  - Suggested response: Role changes are executed via the infra console, stored as audit events (event_type=admin_policy_change) and require two-step approval for production roles (PR in infra repo + approval via gitops pipeline). Approver lists are recorded in the PR metadata.

- Q: "How do you prove an access request was authorized?"
  - Suggested response: Show timeline: authn event (auth.login.success) -> authz decision (authz.decision.allow with role and policy_id) -> resource access event (resource.read). All events share global_request_id and are persisted for 365 days per retention config.

- Q: "What prevents privilege escalation via role overlap?"
  - Suggested response: RBAC v2 enforces least privilege by design, roles are scoped by namespace and a daily job runs a policy-simulate check flagging overlapping permissions which are routed to the security-owner for review.

SIEM queries and examples (copyable):
- Admin policy change (pseudo-sql-like for Elastic):
  POST /_search?pretty
  {
    "query": {
      "bool": {
        "must": [
          { "match": { "event_type": "admin_policy_change" } },
          { "range": { "@timestamp": { "gte": "now-30d" } } }
        ]
      }
    }
  }

- Role assignment across envs (Splunk):
  index=auth_events event_type=role_assignment | stats count by actor, role, environment

Technical acceptance criteria (summary):
- Role-to-control mapping file exists and is referenced in the evidence index.
- >=95% cross-service correlation via global_request_id for a 7-day rolling window.
- SIEM composite dashboard saved and accessible to auditors with read-only tokens.
- Automated evidence collection for Dedicated/Private validated in staging.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Backfilling correlation for historical events may be incomplete.
  - Mitigation: Provide auditor with sampled manual reconstructions and a statement of completeness with confidence bands.

- Risk: On-prem customers with strict air-gapped constraints may not permit scheduled pulls.
  - Mitigation: Support signed, customer-initiated uploads and manual transfer runbook.

Next steps (short-term):
1) Produce role-to-control CSV and README (owner: Maya) — due 2025-11-17.
2) Create SIEM saved queries and dashboard prototype (owner: Jasper) — due 2025-11-24.
3) Implement global_request_id middleware in platform-template and open PRs (owner: Ethan) — initial PRs by 2025-12-01.
4) Schedule customer-run evidence upload beta for 2 Dedicated tenants (owner: Lina) — kickoff 2025-12-08.

Appendix A: sample audit log schema (recommended canonical fields):
- timestamp: ISO8601
- service: string (service-name)
- environment: prod|staging|dedicated|private
- event_type: auth.login.success | authz.decision | admin_policy_change | role_assignment | resource.read|resource.write
- actor: user_id|service_account
- role: role_id
- policy_id: policy identifier (when applicable)
- request_id: global_request_id (correlation id)
- resource_id: optional
- outcome: success|failure
- raw_payload: minimal JSON string of context (encrypted at rest)

Appendix B: checklist for auditor package (evidence index):
- roles-control-mapping.csv (this sprint deliverable)
- saved SIEM dashboard link + read-only token
- 7-day correlation sample export (CSV) with explanation of methodology
- runbook: how evidence was collected (automation steps and manual fallbacks)
- PRs showing policy changes and approvals across the audit period

Notes to reviewers: This doc intentionally mixes sprint language and auditor-friendly outputs. The goal is to turn engineering workstreams into demonstrable artifacts quickly. If want a more formal "auditor handoff pack" I can produce a one-pager and a zipped evidence index with signed manifests after the P0 items land.

End of report.
